source_text: Τοῦτο γάρ ἐστι σύνοδος. Διὰ τοῦτο οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν τοὺς συλλόγους τούτους ἐπέγνωσαν, ἵνα ἃ καθ' ἑκάστην ἡμέραν μαθεῖν οὐ δυνάμεθα, τῇ τῶν διδασκόντων καὶ ὑπομιμνησκόντων ἐνδείᾳ, ταῦτα δι' ἔτους συνιόντες, ἐν κοινῇ πανηγύρει ὑπο δεξώμεθα· εἶτα φυλάξωμεν ἐφόδια πρὸς τὸν ἐφ εξῆς χρόνον, καὶ ἔναυλα ἔχοντες τῇ μνήμῃ τὰ καθ' ἕκαστον, φύγωμεν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν, διώξωμεν δὲ τὸ ἔργον τῆς δικαιοσύνης. «Μὴ μέταιρε ὅρια αἰώνια. Εἰς δὲ κτῆμα ὀρφανῶν μὴ εἰσέλθῃς.» Μὴ προφασίζου τοὺς παῖδας, ὁ πλεονέκτης. Παῖδές εἰσι; θησαύριζε αὐτοῖς θησαυρὸν αἰώνιον. Θησαυρὸς δέ ἐστιν ἡ εὐσέβεια χρημάτων. Κατάλειπε παισὶν ἀγαθὴν μνήμην ἢ πλοῦτον πολύν. Πάντας ποίησαι τοῦ παιδὸς τοῦ σοῦ πατέρας διὰ τῆς εὐποιίας. Ἀνάγκη σέ ποτε ἀπελθεῖν τοῦ βίου· εἶτα τὸν σὸν παῖδα ἐν τῇ ἀφηλικίᾳ καταλείψεις, τῶν προεστώτων δεόμενον. Ἐὰν μὲν γὰρ καλὸς καὶ ἀγαθὸς ᾖς, ἕκαστος τὸν σὸν ἔκγονον ὥσπερ ἴδιον ἐκθρέψει· μεμνήσεται γὰρ, ὅτι καὶ σὺ ὀρφανῶν πατὴρ ἐγένου· ἐὰν δὲ ἐν πονηρίᾳ ζήσας, καὶ πολλοὺς λυπήσας, καὶ παντὸς θηρίου χαλεπώτε ρος γενόμενος τοῖς συντυγχάνουσιν, εἶτα ὑπεξέλθῃς τοῦ βίου, κατέλιπες τὸν σὸν ἔκγονον κοινὸν ἐχθρὸν τῶν ζώντων. Ὥσπερ γὰρ τέκνον σκορπίου ὁ θεασά μενος φοβεῖται, μή ποτε εἰς ἡλικίαν ἐλθὸν μιμήσηται τὸν πατέρα· οὕτω καὶ τὰ σὰ ἔκγονα πονηρίας πα τρικῆς ὄντα κληρονόμα, πρὶν εἰς ἡλικίαν ἐλθεῖν, παρὰ πάντων ἐπιβουλευθήσεται. Τί οὖν πολλοὺς ἐπιβούλους καὶ ἐχθροὺς συνάγεις τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ τέκνοις; Καίτοι, εἰ καὶ πάντα τὸν χρόνον ἔζης, ἔδει σε μᾶλλον τῶν πολλῶν τὴν εὔνοιαν ἔχειν συνεργόν. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ ἄδηλον τὸ κατὰ σὲ, κατάλιπε διὰ τῆς εὐποιίας πολ λοὺς τοὺς προϊσταμένους· μή ποτέ σου ὑπεξελθόν τος, εἶτα τοῦ πλούτου, ὃν συνάγεις, εἰς ὄνησιν μὴ δυνηθέντος διαδεχθῆναι, ἕκαστος κινήσῃ τὴν κε φαλὴν, καὶ εἴπῃ· Πῶς τὰ κακῶς κτηθέντα εἰς ἐκγό νους καὶ παῖδας οὐ παρεπέμφθη; Ταῦτά σοι λέγω ἐκ τῶν ἀνθρωπίνων λόγων· τὰ μέντοι παρὰ τοῦ Κυ ρίου, οἷά σοι ἐρεῖ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον, οἶδας. Μὴ προφασίζου τοὺς παῖδας. Τί ὑποτίθῃ ἀφορ μὴν εὐπρόσωπον εἰς τὴν ἁμαρτίαν; Ὁ τὸν παῖδα ποιήσας, καὶ σὲ ἐποίησεν. Ὁ σοὶ τὰς ἀφορμὰς παρεχόμενος, καὶ τῷ παιδὶ παρέξει τὰς τοῦ βίου διεξαγωγάς. Ἕκαστος τῆς ἑαυτοῦ ζωῆς λόγον δώσει τῷ Κυρίῳ. Τί οἶδας τίνι θησαυρίζεις; «Θησαυρί ζει, καὶ οὐκ οἶδε τίνι συνάξει αὐτά.» Πολλάκις ὁ παῖς ἐστιν ὑπόθεσις τῶν θησαυριζομένων. Ἐγέ νετο δὲ ἢ λῃστοῦ διάρπαγμα, ἢ συκοφάντου παρανάλωμα, ἢ πολεμίων αἰχμαλώτευμα τὰ ὑπὸ σοῦ συν αχθέντα, ἢ λοιμοῦ ἐγκατασκήψαντος. Πολλοὶ γὰρ ἀφανισμοὶ τοῦ βίου. Εἰπέ μοι· ὅτε ᾔτεις παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ τοὺς παῖδας, ὅτε ἐβούλου γενέσθαι τέκνων πα τὴρ, τί προσετίθεις τῇ εὐχῇ; Δός μοι παῖδας, ἵνα, πλεονέκτης γενόμενος, τῇ προφάσει τῶν παίδων τῇ γεέννῃ παραδοθῶ; Δός μοι παῖδας, ἵνα μὴ ποιήσω τὰς ἐντολάς; Δός μοι παῖδας, ἵνα τοῦ Εὐαγγελίου καταφρονήσω; Οὐ ταῦτα ἦν ἃ τότε ἔλεγες, ἀλλὰ παῖδας ἐζήτεις συνεργοὺς τοῦ βίου. Ἔλαβες συνεργοὺς, κοινωνοὺς τοῦ βίου· δίδασκε καὶ λόγοις ἀγαθοῖς, καὶ ὑποδείγμασι χρηστοῖς, ὁποίους προσῆκεν εἶναι τὰ πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν, ὁποίους πολλάκις εἶδες.
thought_title: Children Are No Excuse for Greed
orientation: The preacher attacks greed, telling hearers not to seize orphans property on the plea of providing for their own children.
pass_a_gloss: For this is a gathering. For because of this our fathers acknowledged these meetings, in order that what we are not able to learn on each day, by lack of those teaching and reminding, coming together through a year we may receive in a common festival; then we may keep them as supplies for the coming time, and having each point lodged in memory, we may flee sin, and we may pursue the work of righteousness. Do not move ancient boundaries. And do not enter into property of orphans. Do not use the children as excuse, greedy man. Are there children? Store up for them an eternal treasure. And reverence toward God is treasure of money. Leave behind for children a good remembrance rather than much wealth. Make all men fathers of your child through doing good. It is necessary for you at some time to depart from life; then you will leave your child in youth needing those standing over him. For if you are good and noble, each one will rear your offspring as his own; for he will remember that you also became father of orphans; but if having lived in wickedness, and having grieved many, and having become harsher than every wild beast to those meeting you, then you depart from life, you left your offspring as a common enemy of the living. For just as one seeing offspring of a scorpion fears, lest coming into full age it imitate the father; so also your offspring, being heirs of fatherly wickedness, before coming into full age will be plotted against by all. Why then do you gather many plotters and enemies against your own children? And yet, even if you were to live all the time, you ought rather to have the good will of the many as helper. But since what concerns you is uncertain, leave behind through doing good many protectors; lest ever, when you have departed, and the wealth which you gather has not been able to pass in succession for benefit, each one shake the head, and say: How were things acquired evilly not passed along to offspring and children? These things I say to you from human reasonings; but the things from the Lord, such as the Gospel will say to you, you know. Do not use the children as excuse. Why do you lay down a fair looking occasion for sin? He who made the child, also made you. He who furnishes you occasions, also will furnish to the child the means of carrying on life. Each one will give account of his own life to the Lord. What do you know to whom you store treasure? He stores treasure, and does not know for whom he will gather them. Often the child is the alleged cause of the things stored up. But the things gathered by you became either plunder of a robber, or consumption of a false accuser, or captive prize of enemies, or of a plague having fallen upon them. For many are the disappearances of life. Tell me: when you were asking children from God, when you were wishing to become father of children, what were you adding to the prayer? Give to me children, in order that, having become a greedy man, by the excuse of the children I may be handed over to Gehenna? Give to me children, in order that I may not do the commandments? Give to me children, in order that I may despise the Gospel? Not these were the things which you were saying then, but you were seeking children as helpers of life. You received helpers, sharers of life; teach also by good words, and by worthy examples, what sort they ought to be in things toward God, what sort you often saw.

keeps literal boundary removal image tied to land seizure
keeps literal fair in appearance plus occasion for sin, not a neutral excuse

bible_refs.note: Μὴ μέταιρε ὅρια αἰώνια. Εἰς δὲ κτῆμα ὀρφανῶν μὴ εἰσέλθῃς
Θησαυρίζει, καὶ οὐκ οἶδε τίνι συνάξει αὐτά; LXX 38:7

pass_b_english: This is what gathering means. Our fathers established these meetings for this reason. We cannot learn each day what we need, for want of people to teach us and remind us. So we come together year by year, and we receive it in a common festival. Then we guard it as provision for the time ahead. We keep each point sounding in memory. We flee sin. We pursue the work of righteousness. Scripture says, “Do not move ancient boundaries, and do not enter the field of orphans” (Proverbs 23:10).

You greedy man, do not use your children as an excuse. Do you have children? Store up an eternal treasure for them. Reverence toward God is a treasure of wealth. Leave your children a good memory rather than great wealth. Through doing good, make everyone a father to your child.

You must one day leave this life. Then you will leave your child young and in need of guardians. If you are good and upright, everyone will raise your offspring as his own. Each person will remember that you also became a father to orphans. But if you have lived in wickedness, grieved many people, and grown harsher than any wild beast to those you meet, and then you leave this life, you have left your offspring as a common enemy to the living.

When a man sees the young of a scorpion, he is afraid. He fears it will grow up and copy its father. So it is with your children. They inherit a father’s wickedness. Before they reach adulthood, everyone will plot against them. Why then do you gather many plotters and enemies around your own children? Even if you were to live through all time, you would still need the goodwill of many beside you. Since your own future is uncertain, leave many guardians behind through doing good. Otherwise you will be gone, and the wealth you gather will fail to pass on for any benefit. Then each person will shake his head and say, “How is it that what was wrongly gained did not pass to offspring and children?”

I say this to you from human reasoning. What comes from the Lord, what the Gospel will say to you, you know. Do not use your children as an excuse. Why do you lay down a fair-looking occasion for sin? He who made your child also made you. He who gives you the means to live will also give your child the means to carry on his life. Each person will give an account of his own life to the Lord. What do you know about for whom you store treasure? Scripture says, “He stores up treasure, and does not know for whom he will gather it” (Psalms 39:6). Often a child is only the alleged cause of what is stored. Yet what you gathered becomes plunder for a robber, waste for a slanderer, spoil carried off by enemies, or loss when plague strikes. For the good things of this life vanish in many ways.

Tell me. When you asked God for children, when you wanted to become a father, what did you add to your prayer? Did you say, “Give me children, so that I may become a greedy man and, on the pretext of my children, be handed over to hell”? Did you say, “Give me children, so that I may not keep the commandments”? Did you say, “Give me children, so that I may despise the Gospel”? That is not what you said then. You sought children as helpers for life. You have received helpers and partners in life. So teach them with good words and good examples what sort they should be toward God, the sort you have often seen.
notes: Source file shows spacing splits in many words such as ὑπο δεξώμεθα and ἐφ εξῆς and πα τρικῆς and κε φαλὴν and Κυ ρίου and συν αχθέντα; sense remains clear and gloss follows joined forms

problems.quote: because no one teaches and reminds us
problems.source_quote: τῇ τῶν διδασκόντων καὶ ὑπομιμνησκόντων ἐνδείᾳ
problems.why: ἐνδείᾳ means a shortage of teachers and remind-ers, which the English turns into total absence.
problems.fix: for want of people to teach us and remind us
problems.ruling: τῇ τῶν διδασκόντων καὶ ὑπομιμνησκόντων ἐνδείᾳ means 'for lack/want of teachers and remind-ers'; 'because no one teaches' asserts total absence, overstating it, though meaning is close.

problems.quote: Reverence toward God is treasure set against money.
problems.source_quote: Θησαυρὸς δέ ἐστιν ἡ εὐσέβεια χρημάτων.
problems.why: The Greek identifies piety as the treasure of wealth, and does not set it against money.
problems.fix: Piety is a treasure of wealth.
problems.ruling: Θησαυρὸς ... ἡ εὐσέβεια χρημάτων says piety is the treasure of/in place of riches; 'set against money' invents an opposition not stated, misleading.
